body: Forward test of the valuation-temperature method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.42 (naive base rate 0.48) that: Costco's share price return from 20-Nov-2026 to 30-Jun-2027 beats SPY's price return. Evidence: Yahoo monthly closes: COST $1,102.15 on 20-Nov-2026 — at its all-time high (52-wk $844–1,124) while SPY ($689.81) sits ~12% below its high. Q4 FY26 release (24-Sep-2026): FY26 net sales $297.2bn (+10.1%), comparable sales +8.4% (adjusted +6.6%), digital +20.9%; FY26 EPS $20.76 (Q4 $6.75 incl. a non-recurring $0.15 IEEPA tariff refund benefit) → ~53× trailing EPS. Reasoning: Valuation-temperature test on a 'hot' quality compounder: ~53× earnings at an all-time high while the index is in a drawdown means a lot of defensive premium is already in the price; if markets recover, high-multiple defensives tend to lag. But quality compounders have repeatedly defied this, so we shade only moderately below the base. Resolution: YES if (COST close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 1,102.15) > (SPY close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 689.81). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits; special and regular dividends ignored. Source: Yahoo Finance / Nasdaq closes (COST, SPY). Resolve by 2027-06-30; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: A single US large cap beats SPY over ~7 months a bit under half the time (~48%; skewed single-stock returns).
data.resolution_rule: YES if (COST close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 1,102.15) > (SPY close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 689.81). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits; special and regular dividends ignored.

title: Paper call: Costco's share price return from 20-Nov-2026 to 30-Jun-2027 beats SPY's price return
